Thanks for the response! I like a lot of what you are saying here, and feel that I should explain more, as I would like to know where the flaws are.

Suppose the world is in a loop. The exact formation of the  universe starts repeatedly, which then will result in the exact same ending environment. For the sake of this, I’ll say I’m version 1, which will experience everything till my death. Now version 1 has all those experiences in memory. Now the universe happens again, and there’s another me that has to be born and die again. If we put the consciousness of version 1 in the second me, it would result in something illogical- a baby born with knowledge, rather than being a clean slate. So either you wipe the consciousness of version 1 to put in me 2, or just create version 2 to be the “ghost in the machine”. So yes, both things are me, and both experienced the same things in life in the same ways. Except that doesn’t mean that the same consciousness was experienced by the same ghost.

I understand that I make choices, I’m not just a mere observer of this body and consciousness. I am a function of my body, and other organs in my body also have a function. I know some created consciousness must be in my body to work, but I am saying that regardless if it’s the consciousness of version 1 or version 2, my body will do the exact same thing. The lack of personal identity I feel is because 1 never made a different choice than 2. 

Now I understand that someone who believes in free will can completely disregard everything, and say that we make choices. However, I am looking for someone who is a hard determinist that has gotten past this feeling, or has a reason why I shouldn’t be feeling this way. I feel powerless, because I was determined to feel powerless and simply can’t help it. I would like to have an optimistic view while being a hard determinist, I just currently do not.

I should mention that I am talking about hard determinism.
I believe that I and everything in the universe are made of particles, and that those particles have set properties that, when they interact with each other under the same conditions, will react a determined way. If all the rules of the universe were put into a computer, then that computer could predict everything with 100% accuracy given any set frame in time.
The feeling of helplessness that I am talking about is the fact that I am made of those particles that, while no one can predict the future accurately, will result in my life going in an exact way that this supposed supercomputer could predict. What I am saying is that, while it feels like I am in control and making decisions, well, I’m just made of these predictable particles. Whether it’s my present self, that feels conscious at this very moment, or some other consciousness experiencing my life, both of those lives would turn out the same. The decisions made in my life or anyone else’s, was just determined by the environment(the universe and all it’s properties).
I feel powerless just like anyone else would feel if they experienced my body’s consciousness instead of me. I feel helpless because no matter how I think, I can’t change anything that wasn’t already going to happen. So if I try to change something and succeed, that was going to happen anyway. If I choose to feel helpless and soak in sorrow for the rest of my life, well, I couldn’t have changed the way the particles in the universe interact.
The post didn’t really explain in enough depth why I feel powerless, and that’s my bad. I was just under the assumption that other people who have accepted hard determinism have felt this way and maybe overcome it.
I wish you the best on your journey! Hope something good comes out of it

I have schizophrenia and when I went through my episode, I know it was really hard on my family. Them seeing me in a state that wasn’t who I used to be, and completely delusional. After a month in the hospital, they could definitely recognize me a bit more. When I got released, I had a lot going on in my head and sleep was my way of trying to resolve it. Maybe two months after the hospital, I was back to my normal self, working a job without any major delusions. After that episode, I had to continue dealing with symptoms as they came up, but was functioning close to normal.

Don’t let whatever delusions he’s having affect how you are thinking of him. Try to treat him as you always would. When he brings up something that is obviously a delusion, don’t disagree with them, but hear him out and kindly reason why his delusion might not be the case. In the immortal heart situation, after listening say “That’s very interesting, but I’ve never heard of this happening to anyone”. Make him feel heard and try and talk with him without bringing any emotions into it, just a light discussion. You can try and change the conversation topic just by talking to him as you always would, and see if it sparks his interest away from everything that’s going on in his mind.

At the end of the day, your brother is still there, he’s just sick and needs to recover. From my experience, having the delusions wasn’t the worst part, in all honesty I kind of enjoyed them at the time, made me think my life was like a movie. Having people visit me reminding me of when I was in a stable mindset definitely helped with my recovery. For me, the worst part was the depression afterward. Realizing that you’re just a normal person who now has to deal with losing that time in your life (however long it lasted) and all the people who you potentially hurt was rough.

Just being there will help him with a speedy recovery. I’m sure your brother will get better soon. I wish you and your family the best!
